newsitem.title: UK: UK air cargo industry agrees on import procedures.
newsitem.headline: UK air cargo industry agrees on import procedures.

text.p: The British air cargo industry has reached agreement on key measurement processes for all import transactions, the UK Air Freight Forum (AFF) said after its latest meeting in London.
The forum is made up of 20 shippers (exporters and importers), forwarders and airlines.

Andrew Traill, of shippers' body, the Freight Transport Association and AFF member, told Reuters that the meeting agreed on a standard import measurement code based on the arrival of shipments at an airport and the availability of the necessary documentation and cargo by forwarders.
"This measurement has been defined and the next step will be a timescale, which we hope will be agreed at the next AFF meeting in London on July 1," he said.

He added that AFF would report on its progress to the recently-launched Forum for Air Cargo in Europe (FACE), the first pan-European umbrella body to promote the industry aimed at improving both quality and performance standards for the final customers.

He said he expected that all members of The International Air Cargo Association (TIACA) and International Air Transport Association (IATA) would be kept informed of developments and asked for their input.
"This (imported freight measurement agreement) is something we never had before," said Traill, who is the FTA's shipping and air manager.
He added that progress was made at the meeting towards shippers providing airlines and forwarders with easily understandable export freight delivery information.
"This issue will also come up again at the next meeting," he said.
